Glamdring Research September 28, 2026 13 min 6 sources checked

Lambda’s cheapest GPU instance is a single NVIDIA Quadro RTX 6000 at $0.69 per GPU-hour, on Lambda’s pricing page checked 28 September 2026. 1 The dearest is a single NVIDIA B200 SXM6 at $6.99, and an 8-GPU H100 SXM instance costs $3.99 per GPU-hour. 1 1-Click Clusters cost $5.54 to $6.16 per H100-hour and $8.87 to $9.86 per B200-hour on terms of 2 weeks to 1 year. 1 Every price is before sales tax, VAT or GST. 1

results.title: Nebius sets the cheapest published H100 across the nine providers we track at $3.85 per GPU-hour. It has posted an increase to $4.50 for October 1. | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
# Nebius sets the cheapest published H100 across the nine providers we track at $3.85 per GPU-hour. It has posted an increase to $4.50 for October 1. | Bobby Clay · LinkedIn · 2026-09-29T00:00:00+00:00

**Bobby Clay**.

---

Nebius sets the cheapest published H100 across the nine providers we track at $3.85 per GPU-hour. It has posted an increase to $4.50 for October 1.

Nebius is adding 65 cents to its own rate. The cheapest published H100 across those nine goes up five cents, from $3.85 to $3.90, because Crusoe is next at $3.90 in US East (New York), then Lambda $3.99 in the same September 27 catalog.

Sixty-five cents at one provider, five cents on the board, and Nebius drops from first to third. Nothing else on the published side moved. Not one rate we compared changed more than 1%, and the four floors on our board have not moved since August 24.

The traded market did move. The Ornn Compute Price Index, a third-party index built from actual transactions, settled A100 SXM4 at $0.91 on September 28, the lowest weekly reading we have recorded since May 18. B200 settled at $8.11, the highest.

If you are renewing H100 or A100, that index is your lever. The traded price is now below every rate published across those nine. On H100 it settled at $2.56 against the cheapest rate published across those nine at $3.85, a gap of $1.29 that was $1.06 a week earlier. The list price is not your anchor.

One limit worth stating. A published rate is an asking price and a posted rate is an intention. Our September 27 capture of the Nebius catalog was identical to September 21, so the October 1 rates are published and not yet observed. And the $6.69 B200 listing that sets the floor across those nine is Lambda's, which names no region this week.

Nine providers, every figure dated.

results.title: Best GPU Cloud Providers for AI Startups in 2026: Real H100 and B200 Prices - Startupik
results.author: Ali Hajimohamadi, founder of Startupik
highlights:
One date matters right now. Nebius raises its on-demand prices on 1 October 2026, and most “cheapest GPU” lists have not caught up.

...

- Cheapest single H100: RunPod Secure Cloud H100 SXM at $3.49 per hour, billed by the second, per RunPod’s pricing page.
- Price change to plan for: Nebius H100 goes from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour on 1 October 2026, and B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, per Nebius’s price page.
- Cheapest verified B200: Modal at $6.25 per hour of GPU time, followed by Lambda at $6.69.
- Best commitment discount with a public rate card: Together AI H100 falls from $3.99 on demand to $3.19 on a 91–180 day reservation.
- Minimum-unit trap: CoreWeave sells H100 only as an 8-GPU node at $49.24 per hour, which is $35,945 for a month of 24/7 use.
- Biggest free credits: Google for Startups offers up to $350,000 for AI startups, but only $250,000 of it lands in year one.

...

We read every provider’s official pricing page in September 2026. Where a price is listed per node, we divided it by the GPU count and show both. Where a provider does not publish a price, we say so instead of estimating.

H100 here means the NVIDIA H100 80GB SXM part unless noted. B200 is NVIDIA’s Blackwell data-centre GPU. A neocloud is a GPU-first cloud provider, such as Lambda or CoreWeave, as opposed to a general hyperscaler like AWS.

...

## GPU Cloud Comparison Table: H100 and B200 Prices

| Provider | H100 on-demand (per GPU-hr) | B200 on-demand (per GPU-hr) | Smallest unit | Egress | Self-serve? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RunPod (Secure Cloud) | $3.49 | $6.79 | 1 GPU | Free | Yes |
| Nebius | $3.85 (to $4.50 on 1 Oct) | $7.15 (to $8.50 on 1 Oct) | 1 GPU | $0.015/GiB (Standard object storage) | Yes, up to 32 GPUs |
| Crusoe | $3.90 | Sales only | Not stated | Free | H100/H200 yes |
| Modal | $3.95 + CPU and memory | $6.25 + CPU and memory | Per second, per function | Not stated | Yes |
| Lambda | $3.99 | $6.69 | 1 GPU | Free | Yes |
| Together AI | $3.99 | $8.19 | 8-GPU cluster | Free (per its GA blog) | Yes |
| CoreWeave | $6.16 ($49.24 per 8-GPU node) | $8.60 ($68.80 per node) | 8 GPUs | Free | Yes |
| AWS Capacity Blocks | $5.19 ($41.528 per p5.48xlarge) | $12.36 ($98.84 per p6-b200) | 8 GPUs, paid upfront | First 100 GB/month free | Yes |
| Google Cloud A3 High | $11.06 ($88.49 per 8-GPU VM) | A4 on-demand listed as N/A | 8 GPUs | Standard GCP rates | Yes |
| Nscale | Not published | Not published | Quote | Not published | No |

Prices are US or North America list prices, excluding sales tax or VAT. Google’s figure includes vCPU, memory and local SSD bundled into the VM price.

...

### 2. Lambda: Cleanest Rate Card, No Egress Fees

Why it works: Lambda lists H100 SXM at $3.99 and B200 at $6.69 per GPU-hour, with 1x, 2x, 4x and 8x instance sizes. It advertises “No egress fees” and bills by the minute. For moving large checkpoints and datasets, zero egress is worth more than a 50-cent price gap.

When it breaks: Lambda’s multi-node 1-Click Clusters are priced above its single instances. An HGX B200 cluster costs $9.86 per GPU-hour at 16 GPUs, $9.36 at 64 and $8.87 at 256+, on 2-week to 1-year terms. That is 33% to 47% more than the $6.69 on-demand B200. Lambda’s page does not explain the gap, so ask what networking and support you get before signing.

Use it if you want simple per-GPU pricing and move a lot of data. Skip it if you need spot pricing; Lambda lists none.

### 3. Nebius: Strong Today, Repriced on 1 October

Why it works: Nebius offers self-serve access up to 32 GPUs with “no waitlists or minimum commitments”, after a $25 top-up. It publishes preemptible prices from $0.79 for H100 and H200 and from $0.99 for B200 and B300, the lowest spot entry points in this list.

When it breaks: The new rate card takes effect on 1 October 2026:

- H100: $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%)
- H200: $4.50 to $5.40 (+20%)
- B200: $7.15 to $8.50 (+19%)
- B300: $7.85 to $9.50 (+21%)

After the change, Nebius H100 is more expensive than Lambda, Together and RunPod on demand. Nebius is also the only provider here with a published egress fee: $0.015 per GiB for Standard object storage. Its startup credits are “currently available exclusively through” partner VC funds, for companies with $5M+ raised.

results.title: Lambda Review, Pricing & Alternatives | Saaskly
highlights: Prices are in US dollars, VAT not stated, read 22 September 2026. Lambda charges per GPU per hour, and the rate goes up as you take fewer GPUs, which is the opposite of what most buyers expect. One H100 SXM 80 GB costs $4.29 an hour, or $3,132 a month at 730 hours. Take the whole eight-GPU node and the same GPU costs $3.99 an hour, so the node is $31.92 an hour and each GPU works out at $2,913 a month. Two and four GPU configurations sit in between at $4.19 and $4.09. An H100 PCIe is $3.29 an hour. The cheapest GPU on the list is a Quadro RTX 6000 24 GB at $0.69 an hour, about $504 a month, and a GH200 is $2.29. No H200 appears on the public price list at all, despite the pricing page's own marketing copy mentioning it. There is no spot, preemptible or interruptible tier, so there is no cheap way to buy compute you are willing to lose. Reserved pricing for a single on-demand instance is sales only: no rate, no term and no discount figure is published.

results.title: How much does it cost to rent an H100 per hour?
results.author: The Hardware Desk
highlights:
An Nvidia H100 SXM rented for $2.68 per GPU-hour on 2026-08-26 on Ornn Data’s blended compute price index, while the same chip’s own on-demand list price at Lambda Labs sat at $3.99, and a reserved AWS Capacity Block ran $5.191. All three numbers describe the identical piece of silicon. The one skill this post hands you: read an H100 quote and know which of three separable factors, node granularity, commitment length, or provider tier, explains why it isn’t the number you saw on a different site last week.

...

There is no single H100 price, only a spread that runs roughly $1.87 to $7 per GPU-hour depending on who you ask and what you’re buying. Ornn Data’s blended index put H100 SXM at $2.68 per GPU-hour on 2026-08-26, down 8.5% over the trailing week. Lambda Labs’ own pricing page lists an 8-GPU SXM node at $3.99 per GPU-hour on-demand, rising to $4.29 for a lone GPU, while AWS prices a prepaid EC2 Capacity Block at $5.191 per GPU-hour in US East and US West as of a 2026-08-16 survey. RunPod’s SXM pods listed at $3.29 the same day, and Vast.ai’s peer-to-peer marketplace floor dropped as low as $1.87. None of these figures is wrong; they’re pricing different products (spot marketplace capacity, on-demand branded cloud, prepaid reserved capacity) that happen to run on the same chip.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

## The disclosure and our analysis

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

This is not the first increase. The Motley Fool reports that in early May, Nebius's pricing page showed H100 at $2.95 per hour and B300 at $6.10. [2] Our own catalog recorded H100 at $3.85 on September 18 and B300 at $7.85 on September 24.

...

### How the new rates compare

We compared the new rates with published on demand rates in our provider catalog, checked September 18 to 28.

H100: At $4.50, Nebius moves above Runpod ($3.49), Crusoe ($3.90) and Lambda ($4.29). It stays below CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance, about $6.16 per GPU.

H200: At $5.40, Nebius moves above Runpod ($4.59) and Verda ($4.55). It stays below Together AI ($5.99) and CoreWeave (about $6.31 per GPU).

B200: At $8.50, Nebius moves well above Lambda ($6.69) and Runpod ($6.79). CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance works out to about $8.60 per GPU.

B300: At $9.50, Nebius moves above Verda ($8.20) and Scaleway ($7.50). Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

### What to do before October 1

Ask about locking today's rate. Ask Nebius whether a commitment signed before October 1 is priced at the current rate. Get the answer in writing, with the rate and term.

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

If you have a Nebius quote in hand, ask which rate it uses. A quote issued in September may still show the old price.
